mainQuestionText: You are asked to determine the spring constant (k) of a helical spring by plotting a graph of extension against load. In the experimental setup shown in the figure, one end of the spring is attached to a scale pan and the other end is firmly connected to a stand. Assume that the masses of the scale pan and the spring are negligible.

subQuestions.text: Using the graph drawn above determine the value of k in SI units.
subQuestions.answer:
Gradient = 6.0−0.8 / 300−40 = 5.2 / 260
(Students can select any two points lying on the graph to determine the gradient; disregard the units of the numerator and the denominator)
Identifying k = g / gradient OR [OR 1 / gradient]
k = 50 N m⁻¹ (OR 50 kg s⁻²)
(For correct value and the correct unit)
[Value correct, unit incorrect – 01 mark]

subQuestions.text: Write down two essential experimental steps that you have to follow when taking readings.
subQuestions.answer:
(1) Loading of masses must be done gently OR readings should be noted only when the pointer comes to rest/equilibrium.
(2) The masses should be placed at the center of the pan.
(3) Pointer should not touch the metre ruler OR the pointer should move above/over the ruler OR pointer should not be far away/should be close to the metre ruler.
(4) Record the corresponding readings of the pointer while loading and unloading (and take their average)
(5) Look straight through the pointer when taking readings OR take readings without parallax errors.
(6) The extension of the spring should not exceed the proportional limit.
(Any two correct steps – 01 mark)

subQuestions.text: To maintain the percentage error of k within 5% what should be the maximum error (Δk) of the value of k?
subQuestions.answer:
Δk / 50 x 100 = 5
(for the correct expression or substitution)
Δk = 2.5 N m⁻¹
[When awarding this mark, disregard the unit]
